messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo next steps: HelioData k6 run & SLO clarifications

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your customer-led k6 window scheduled and productive: 

1) Acceptance SLOs we heard in the call:
   - p95 latency target: <= 300ms (in-region, request/response endpoints)
   - Sustained throughput target: 250 req/s for the conversation endpoint for the 30-minute steady-state window
   - Peak concurrency: 180 concurrent streaming sessions (clients holding websocket-like streams)

Please confirm any of the numbers above that are off — particularly whether you need p99 instead of p95 for audit.

2) Test artifacts we need from HelioData for the run:
   - k6 script(s) or a reference subset to exercise both streaming and request/response flows (token refresh logic included)
   - Test account API key(s) scoped to a non-prod project (we recommend time-limited keys)
   - IP ranges to allowlist for the testing agents (we can provide our NAT IPs if you prefer)
   - Preferred test windows (two candidate windows from your side, with time zone)

3) What Redwood will provide:
   - k6 template + small helper script to show token refresh and Keep-Alive handling (attached k6-templates.zip)
   - IP allowlist template (attached ip-allowlist-template.txt) and our egress IP ranges for the agents
   - A short runbook for streaming probes (how we measure open connections, how to compute concurrency vs in-flight requests)

4) Logistics:
   - We recommend a dry run 48 hours before the official window to validate scripts and allowlist entries.
   - Please share a Drive folder where HelioData will drop k6 result artifacts (json/csv) and any console logs; we’ll do the same.

If that all sounds good I’ll drop our agent IP ranges and a suggested dry-run date (Wed, Dec 2, 09:00-10:30 PT) and the proposed official window (Thu, Dec 3, 15:00-16:00 PT).

Thanks — looking forward to validating throughput and streaming concurrency with you.

— Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. This matches what we discussed with a couple clarifications below: 

- For compliance we want p99 for the admin endpoints but p95 for the main conversation path — so split those two SLOs. Can we meet p95 = 300ms for conversation and p99 = 800ms for admin APIs?
- Sustained throughput target is correct; we may need to add a short spike to 350 req/s for a 3-minute blast to simulate a campaign burst.
- Streaming concurrency: 180 is our target but for the dry run we’ll emulate 120 concurrent streams then ramp to 180 during the official test.

We attached our current k6 script bundle and a short README (link below) — the scripts include our client-side token refresh but not the Keep-Alive tweaks you mentioned.

HelioData can provide the following:
- Test API key (time-limited) for the non-prod tenant — I’ll have Ops send credentials via the secure channel by EOD.
- IP allowlist: we’ll add Redwood agent ranges but please send the exact CIDRs you’ll be hitting from.
- Preferred windows: Dec 3, 15:00-16:30 PT (official); dry run: Dec 2, 09:00-10:30 PT. Both work.

Thanks Samantha — that all looks good and the windows work for our team. Two technical clarifications before the dry run: 

1) Streaming sessions vs long-poll: our runtime treats streaming as long-lived websocket-like sessions. For the k6 script: please ensure the ramp-up includes an explicit open connection phase (we count open handles separately from request rate) and that the 3-minute burst is applied to the request rate within existing streams rather than opening 350 new streams. We'll share a small helper that toggles in-stream request bursts.

2) Keep-Alive + Token refresh: if your current k6 bundle re-creates a client per request we recommend modifying it to reuse the client and inject token refresh calls on 401s. The attached k6-templates.zip contains a snippet (scripts/keepalive_and_refresh.js) showing token refresh + connection reuse.

3) IP ranges: our outbound NAT ranges for the Redwood k6 agents are: 54.142.12.0/24, 52.18.95.0/24, 35.153.200.0/24. Please add those CIDRs to your allowlist. (If you prefer we can give per-test fixed IPs for the official window — let me know.)

4) Reporting: please drop raw k6 results (json) into the Drive folder you shared; we’ll collect and run the Redwood post-run analysis (latency histograms, concurrency breakdowns, token expiry traces). Also helpful: the k6 summary.csv and any agent logs.

We’ve tentatively scheduled the dry run Dec 2 09:00-10:30 PT and official run Dec 3 15:00-16:30 PT. Naomi will be the on-call engineer during the runs and Priyom will cover post-run analysis.

— Marcus
